description: Eighth Graders and Emergency Preparedness in Oklahoma is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by City of Miami, Oklahoma; Adaptation International; Institute for Social and Environmental Transition-International. Educating local middle-schoolers about emergency preparedness allows the small city of Miami to build climate resilience in an accessible way and broach the topic of climate change. Coverage: Oklahoma (2017). The toolkit gives Oklahoma as the location, 2017 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

outcomes: For a city that likely had not discussed climate change prior to this project, the approach used by the project team provided an accessible, community-oriented solution that allowed it to move forward and increase resilience within a familiar emergency management framework. Addressing current concerns around extreme weather events in this manner can build resilience without specifically addressing climate change.
